analysis:
The changed file is CHANGELOG.md, documentation only. The supplied patch edits lines 11-25 on the head side: it adds a v0.10.3 candidate section about an M5 Metal-kernel crash fix and bumps the MLX submodule pins (libs/mlx-swift, libs/mlx, nested mlx). The two units I was given (head lines 992-1460) are unchanged historical release notes. I found no new security-relevant behavior in them. The changelog describes no change to attestation, App Attest authorization, key custody, encrypted prefix-cache storage (T-041), fan helper, or coordinator WebSocket contract. Nothing in these units alters TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010 or TB-011 assumptions. The historical text correctly keeps limitations (no activation or qualification claims, SEC-035 accepted risk unchanged).

Coverage limits: the patch excerpt is truncated and the actual submodule pin changes (MLX at 31f550af, mlx-swift at 4926d3d9) are not in the supplied evidence. The changelog says the MLX update is a kernel-argument correction, but I cannot verify that from the supplied diff. A changed numerical or GPU kernel path in MLX could affect inference correctness, or the isolation behavior described in T-028/T-056, and that needs source-level review of the submodule diffs if those are in scope. Because the claim is unverified rather than shown to be a regression, I record it as a question instead of a finding. Also, the claim that a crash-looping provider auto-updates via watchdog relates to T-043 (watchdog authority), but it describes pre-existing behavior and not a new change.
